title: Telemetry linter: metric hygiene & pre-ingest validation for inference KPIs
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build a lightweight 'metric linter' service that validates and enforces metric hygiene for inference KPIs before they are committed to the ingestion path (OTel/protobuf -> ingest gateway -> Prometheus / TSDB). The linter will operate both as a pre-ingest admission filter for agent-side telemetry proxies and as a CI/SDK check developers can run locally. The goal is to reduce cardinality explosions, unify label semantics (model/route/tenant), normalize units and histogram buckets, and produce actionable errors/suggestions rather than silent drops. This reduces downstream storage costs and SLO noise and makes dashboarding and alerts more reliable.
acceptance_criteria: A standalone linter binary (metric-lint) that accepts OTLP/Prometheus metric proto payloads and produces a validation report with severity levels (error/warn/info)

Rules implemented: required label sets for inference requests (model, model_version, route, tenant), maximum cardinality policy per label, allowed label whitelist/denylist, unit normalization (ms/seconds), histogram bucketing policy and exemplar presence
Pre-ingest integration: validate path in ingest proxy flow that can reject or mutate (hint-only mode) metrics with a configurable policy and fallthrough behavior
SDK/CI integration: provide a GitHub Actions step that runs metric-lint against a test payload or instrumentation snapshot and fails on P1 errors
Documentation: PRD + runbook with decision criteria for when to accept, reject, or transform metrics and how to onboard teams
Performance: end-to-end validation added to proxy adds <2ms p95 per request in benchmarked synthetic load for typical payload sizes
Monitoring: linter emits its own telemetry (validation_error_count, auto_fix_count, rule_hit_count) and a dashboard to track policy violations over time
plan: Phase 1: Design rule set and failure modes (3 days) — consult PM/Console/SDK teams and gather common anti-patterns
Phase 2: Prototype CLI linter that reads OTLP/Prometheus payloads and runs rule engine (5 days)
Phase 3: Integrate with ingest proxy as a module (hint-only mode first) and add configuration API (7 days)
Phase 4: Build GitHub Action and SDK hooks for local/CI validation (3 days)
Phase 5: Pilot with two internal teams (console metrics and dedicated runtime) and iterate rules (2 cycles)
Phase 6: Release policy dashboard, docs, and runbook; roll to enforce mode after pilot (stretch)
Post-launch: Collect violation telemetry and propose automated fixes or SDK changes where patterns repeat
notes: Tradeoffs: strict enforcement reduces noisy cardinality but risks breaking teams that rely on high-cardinality tags for experimentation. We'll start in hint-only mode and provide migration guidance.
Implementation language: Go for minimal binary size and easy integration with existing ingest proxy (also Go). Consider a Rust variant if performance requires.
Rule authoring: implement rules as declarative YAML with examples and auto-generated docs. This allows product/observability engineers to tune policies without code changes.
Future work: automatic repair suggestions committed as PRs to team repos, SDK auto-instrumentation templates, and integration with rollout policies for metrics-based canaries.
